name: Procyclidine
metabolism: Absorbed well enough from the gut, with 75% reaching the blood, and it leaves the tissues quickly. There is no detailed information on how procyclidine is broken down, but very little of it comes out unchanged in the urine. Taken by mouth, about a fifth of the dose is known to be broken down in the liver, mostly by cytochrome P450 and then joined to glucuronic acid; that joined-up product has been found in the urine. The body clears it slowly, at 68 ml/min, mostly by breaking it down, with only a little lost on the first pass through the gut wall. It stays in the body for about 12 hours after a dose by mouth.
summary: Procyclidine is an anticholinergic used for drug-induced parkinsonism, akathisia, acute dystonia, Parkinson's disease, and other forms of dystonia.
